The mastic tree bleeds when you cut it, and what comes out hardens into a clear resin the Greeks call the tears of Chios. Growers cut the bark by hand every few days from July through October. The tree seals each wound, the drops fall onto the swept ground, and they cure in the sun until they are solid enough to pick up.
